title: Ezekiel Chapter 24 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 24 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 24 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 24.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 24, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem
The word of the LORD came unto me
Write thee the name of the day
Set on a pot
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto me
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Ezekiel 24:1.

questions.question: What command does the LORD give in Ezekiel 24:2?
options: Write thee the name of the day
Gather the pieces thereof
Burn also the bones
Make the pile for fire great
questions.correctAnswer: Write thee the name of the day
questions.explanation: The command to write the name of the day is specifically stated in Ezekiel 24:2.

questions.question: What does the LORD say to set on in Ezekiel 24:3?
options: A fire
A pot
A stone
A table
questions.correctAnswer: A pot
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly mentions to 'Set on a pot' as stated in Ezekiel 24:3.

questions.question: What should be gathered into the pot according to Ezekiel 24:4?
options: Every good piece
Only the bones
The blood
The ashes
questions.correctAnswer: Every good piece
questions.explanation: The instruction to gather 'every good piece' is found in Ezekiel 24:4.

questions.question: What type of bones does the LORD command to fill the pot with in Ezekiel 24:4?
options: Choice bones
Unclean bones
Old bones
Fresh bones
questions.correctAnswer: Choice bones
questions.explanation: The text specifically mentions 'choice bones' in Ezekiel 24:4.

questions.question: What city is referred to as the 'bloody city' in Ezekiel 24:6?
options: Jerusalem
Babylon
Egypt
Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The phrase 'bloody city' refers to Jerusalem as stated in Ezekiel 24:6.

questions.question: What does the LORD say should not be done to the scum in Ezekiel 24:6?
options: Let it remain
Go out of it
Be burned
Be covered
questions.correctAnswer: Go out of it
questions.explanation: The verse specifies that the scum is 'not gone out of it' in Ezekiel 24:6.

questions.question: Where did she set her blood according to Ezekiel 24:7?
options: On the ground
On the top of a rock
In the pot
In the water
questions.correctAnswer: On the top of a rock
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:7 clearly states that 'she set it upon the top of a rock.'

questions.question: What did the LORD say about the blood in Ezekiel 24:8?
options: It should be covered
It should not be covered
It should be poured out
It should be washed away
questions.correctAnswer: It should not be covered
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says that 'it should not be covered' in Ezekiel 24:8.

questions.question: What does the LORD promise to do to the bloody city in Ezekiel 24:9?
options: Make a pile for fire great
Cover it with dust
Bring peace
Destroy its walls
questions.correctAnswer: Make a pile for fire great
questions.explanation: The promise made is to 'make the pile for fire great' as stated in Ezekiel 24:9.

questions.question: The king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem on which day?
options: The first day
The second day
This same day
The last day
questions.correctAnswer: This same day
questions.explanation: According to Ezekiel 24:2, this event occurred 'this same day.'

questions.question: Is it true that the word of the LORD came unto Ezekiel?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text states that 'the word of the LORD came unto me' in Ezekiel 24:1.

questions.question: Is it true that the bloody city refers to Babylon?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Although it is not explicitly stated in the text, the context of 'the bloody city' refers to Jerusalem, not Babylon, making the statement false.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD commanded to cover the blood with dust?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not state that the LORD commanded to cover the blood with dust; rather, it mentions that the blood was 'not covered' in Ezekiel 24:8.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD asked Ezekiel to set a table?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention anything about setting a table; it discusses setting on a pot as stated in Ezekiel 24:3.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 24 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 24 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 24:10, what should be done to the flesh?
options: Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned
Cover the flesh with water and bury it
Wash the flesh and anoint it with oil
Cut the flesh into pieces and scatter it
questions.correctAnswer: Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh, and spice it well, and let the bones be burned
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:10 commands to heap wood, kindle fire, consume the flesh, spice it well, and burn the bones, indicating a complete and consuming fire.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 24:14 promise will happen if someone is not purged from filthiness as commanded in Ezekiel 24:13?
options: God will not go back, spare, or repent; judgment will come according to their ways and doings
They will be immediately cleansed by fire
They will receive mercy and forgiveness
They will be left alone without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God will not go back, spare, or repent; judgment will come according to their ways and doings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14 states that God will not relent or spare; their judgment will correspond to their ways and doings as a consequence of not being purged in 24:13.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 24:11, what is the purpose of setting the pot empty upon the coals?
options: So that the brass of it may be hot, burn, and the filthiness may be molten and consumed
To cool down the pot after boiling
To cover the pot and stop the fire
To wash the pot thoroughly
questions.correctAnswer: So that the brass of it may be hot, burn, and the filthiness may be molten and consumed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:11 explains the pot is set on coals to heat the brass and melt away the filthiness and scum, symbolizing purification by fire.

questions.question: How do Ezekiel 24:12 and Ezekiel 24:13 connect in describing the condition and future of the city?
options: Verse 12 shows the city’s lies and scum remain, and verse 13 declares it will not be purged until God's fury rests
Verse 12 promises forgiveness, and verse 13 predicts restoration
Verse 12 foretells peace, and verse 13 warns of war
Verse 12 and 13 both describe the city's prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 12 shows the city’s lies and scum remain, and verse 13 declares it will not be purged until God's fury rests
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:12 mentions the great scum remains despite weariness with lies, and 24:13 declares no purging from filthiness until God’s fury rests on it.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be drawn from Ezekiel 24:16 about dealing with personal loss?
options: One must not mourn or weep publicly even when losing someone dear
One should express all emotions openly and loudly
One should isolate themselves completely
One should immediately seek revenge
questions.correctAnswer: One must not mourn or weep publicly even when losing someone dear
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16 commands the prophet not to mourn or weep despite loss, teaching restraint in grief as part of obedience and submission to God’s will.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 24:17, what specific actions does God command regarding mourning customs?
options: Forbear to cry, make no mourning, bind the tire on the head, put on shoes, cover not lips, and do not eat bread of men
Cry loudly, tear clothes, sit on the ground, and fast for seven days
Burn incense, offer sacrifices, and shout in the streets
Wear sackcloth, cover head with ashes, and remain silent
questions.correctAnswer: Forbear to cry, make no mourning, bind the tire on the head, put on shoes, cover not lips, and do not eat bread of men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:17 commands specific mourning customs to be avoided or followed, emphasizing controlled behavior during grief as part of prophetic obedience.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 24:12 say about the city’s scum and lies?
options: She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her: her scum shall be in the fire
She is innocent and cleansed from all sins
She is blessed and will prosper abundantly
Her scum was removed by the people’s repentance
questions.correctAnswer: She hath wearied herself with lies, and her great scum went not forth out of her: her scum shall be in the fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:12 describes the city as wearying itself with lies, with scum that remains and will be consumed by fire, symbolizing impending judgment.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:10-11 illustrate God’s method of purging sin in practical terms?
options: Through consuming fire that cleanses flesh and burns away filthiness and scum
By washing with water and anointing with oil
Through gentle rebuke and forgiveness
By ignoring sin and waiting for repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Through consuming fire that cleanses flesh and burns away filthiness and scum
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 describe a process of burning flesh and melting filthiness by fire, symbolizing God’s purifying judgment on sin.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 24:14 reveal about God’s nature in executing judgment?
options: God will not go back, spare, or repent but will execute judgment according to people’s ways and doings
God is easily swayed to mercy and often changes His mind
God does not judge but leaves people to their own devices
God only judges after repeated warnings and second chances
questions.correctAnswer: God will not go back, spare, or repent but will execute judgment according to people’s ways and doings
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14 emphasizes God’s steadfastness and justice in judgment without relenting, matching consequences to actions.

questions.question: How might the instruction in Ezekiel 24:17 about not eating the bread of men be understood in a practical Christian living context?
options: Avoid participating in customary social rituals that contradict God’s commands during times of judgment
Eat as much bread as possible to show strength
Share bread generously with others
Ignore all customs and act freely
questions.correctAnswer: Avoid participating in customary social rituals that contradict God’s commands during times of judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:17’s prohibition against eating the bread of men during mourning reflects the call to obedience and separation from worldly customs that contradict God’s will.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 24:16 teach about emotional discipline in the face of personal tragedy?
options: One should restrain mourning and tears as an act of obedience to God’s command
One should express grief without restraint
One should seek comfort from others immediately
One should forget the tragedy quickly
questions.correctAnswer: One should restrain mourning and tears as an act of obedience to God’s command
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16 commands the prophet not to mourn or weep despite losing his wife, illustrating emotional discipline and submission to God’s purpose.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:15-18 demonstrate the prophet’s obedience to God's command amidst personal loss?
options: Ezekiel did not mourn or weep when his wife died, obeying God's instructions exactly
Ezekiel mourned loudly and publicly
Ezekiel fled from his duties
Ezekiel sought revenge for his loss
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel did not mourn or weep when his wife died, obeying God's instructions exactly
questions.explanation: Verses 15-18 show Ezekiel receiving God’s word, then obeying by not mourning publicly when his wife died, modeling faith and obedience amid suffering.

questions.question: What is the significance of the pot and the fire metaphor in Ezekiel 24:3-9 in relation to the primary verses 10-14?
options: The pot and fire symbolize God’s judgment consuming the city’s sin, which is detailed in 10-14 as consuming flesh and scum
The pot is a symbol of peace and restoration
The fire represents God’s mercy and kindness
The pot is a metaphor for the temple and worship
questions.correctAnswer: The pot and fire symbolize God’s judgment consuming the city’s sin, which is detailed in 10-14 as consuming flesh and scum
questions.explanation: The earlier verses (3-9) set the metaphor of a pot boiling with pieces causing scum, which 10-14 clarify as judgment by fire consuming sin and filthiness.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was commanded to mourn and publicly show grief for his wife’s death according to Ezekiel 24:16-17.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16-17 explicitly commands the prophet not to mourn or weep and to avoid typical mourning customs, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel 24:14 says God will repent and spare the people if they change their ways.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14 states God will not go back, spare, or repent, but will judge according to their ways and doings, making the statement false.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 24 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 24.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 24:21, what does the Lord say He will profane?
options: My sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes
The temple, the altar, and the holy place
The land and the trees thereof
The mountains and the rivers
questions.correctAnswer: My sanctuary, the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:21 specifically states that the Lord will profane His sanctuary, the excellency of their strength, the desire of their eyes, and that which their soul pitieth.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 24:22, what are the people instructed to do as Ezekiel did?
options: Not cover their lips, nor eat the bread of men
Build an altar and offer sacrifices
Gather the people and proclaim a fast
Wear sackcloth and ashes
questions.correctAnswer: Not cover their lips, nor eat the bread of men
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:22 commands the people to do as Ezekiel did: not to cover their lips nor eat the bread of men, symbolizing the cessation of mourning rituals.

questions.question: What symbolic attire does Ezekiel say the people will wear in Ezekiel 24:23?
options: Their tires upon their heads, and shoes upon their feet
Cloaks of sackcloth and sandals
Shirts of hair and sandals
Crowns of thorns and sandals
questions.correctAnswer: Their tires upon their heads, and shoes upon their feet
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:23 describes the people wearing their tires upon their heads and shoes upon their feet, indicating a mourning without the usual signs of weeping or lamentation.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 24:24, what is Ezekiel described as being to the people?
options: A sign
A prophet
A priest
A judge
questions.correctAnswer: A sign
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:24 declares that Ezekiel is a sign to the people; what he has done, they shall do, and through this they shall know that He is the Lord GOD.

questions.question: What will happen to those who escape on the day of judgment according to Ezekiel 24:26?
options: They shall come to Ezekiel to cause him to hear it with his ears
They shall rebuild the temple
They shall be taken to captivity
They shall be anointed kings
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come to Ezekiel to cause him to hear it with his ears
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:26 says that those who escape on that day shall come to Ezekiel to cause him to hear the news, signifying the transmission of the devastation's account.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 24:27, what will happen to Ezekiel's mouth on the day the escaped come to him?
options: His mouth shall be opened and he shall speak, no longer dumb
He shall remain silent
He shall prophesy in unknown tongues
He shall weep silently
questions.correctAnswer: His mouth shall be opened and he shall speak, no longer dumb
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:27 states that on that day Ezekiel’s mouth shall be opened, and he shall speak and be no longer dumb, becoming a sign to the people.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'yare' (יִרְאֶה) in Ezekiel 24:26 most accurately mean?
options: To cause to see or hear
To build or construct
To hide or conceal
To destroy or consume
questions.correctAnswer: To cause to see or hear
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'yare' in Ezekiel 24:26 is commonly understood to mean 'to cause to see or hear', fitting the context where the escaped come to cause Ezekiel to hear the news.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Ezekiel 24:3-6 with the pot and cooking imagery?
options: Allegory
Chiasmus
Hyperbole
Parable
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:3-6 uses the imagery of a cooking pot as a parable representing Jerusalem’s impending destruction, a common prophetic technique to convey judgment.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of a prophet being a sign as Ezekiel is in Ezekiel 24:24?
options: Matthew 12:39
John 1:29
Acts 2:17
Revelation 1:1
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 12:39
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:39 records Jesus referring to the 'sign of Jonah' as a prophetic sign like Ezekiel’s role, linking prophetic signs to revelation and recognition of God’s work.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage foreshadows the judgment imagery found in Ezekiel 24:6-9?
options: Jeremiah 19:11
Genesis 6:17
Exodus 12:12
Isaiah 53:5
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 19:11
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 19:11 uses the imagery of breaking a potter’s vessel as a metaphor for judgment, similar to Ezekiel’s pot and fire imagery in 24:6-9.

questions.question: What immediately precedes Ezekiel's wife’s death according to Ezekiel 24:18?
options: Ezekiel is commanded not to mourn or weep
The fall of Jerusalem
The king of Babylon setting against Jerusalem
The gathering of the people
questions.correctAnswer: Ezekiel is commanded not to mourn or weep
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16-17 commands Ezekiel not to mourn or weep, and verse 18 then states that his wife died and he obeyed the command, showing the sequence.

questions.question: What Hebrew literary device is illustrated by Ezekiel's personal tragedy paralleling the fate of Jerusalem in Ezekiel 24:15-24?
options: Typology
Alliteration
Simile
Anthropomorphism
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The narrative in Ezekiel 24 uses typology by having Ezekiel’s personal loss symbolically represent Jerusalem’s coming destruction, a prophetic foreshadowing method.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:13 reflect the concept of divine judgment in the Hebrew prophetic tradition?
options: It declares the city will not be purged until God’s fury rests upon it
It promises immediate forgiveness upon repentance
It speaks of a temporary exile followed by restoration
It calls for a human mediator to intercede
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the city will not be purged until God’s fury rests upon it
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:13 states that the city will not be purged of its filthiness until God’s fury rests upon it, affirming the irrevocable nature of divine judgment until fulfilled.

questions.question: True or False: Ezekiel was allowed to mourn and weep openly when his wife died as per the LORD's command.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16-17 commands Ezekiel not to mourn nor weep when his wife died, and he obeyed by not covering his lips or eating the bread of men, symbolic of mourning rituals.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ezekiel 24:14, the LORD will repent and spare Jerusalem if they repent.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14 explicitly states that the LORD will not go back, spare, nor repent but will judge according to their ways and doings.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 24 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 24 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 24:6 teach about human sin?
options: Sin is deeply ingrained and must be removed piece by piece
Sin is easily forgiven by God without judgment
Human sin is superficial and quickly cleansed
Sin has no impact on the communal body of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is deeply ingrained and must be removed piece by piece
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:6 uses the imagery of removing scum from the pot piece by piece, symbolizing that sin is deeply embedded and must be thoroughly purged.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 24:14 teach about God's nature?
options: God is immutable and will not repent from His declared judgment
God frequently changes His mind based on human repentance
God's judgment is conditional and reversible
God is uncertain about the future and may delay judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God is immutable and will not repent from His declared judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14 explicitly states God will not go back, spare, or repent, affirming divine immutability in executing judgment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 24:16 teach about sanctification in times of suffering?
options: Believers are called to obedience even when natural emotions are suppressed
True sanctification allows full expression of grief without restraint
Suffering is irrelevant to sanctification
God demands constant joyful worship regardless of circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to obedience even when natural emotions are suppressed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16 commands Ezekiel not to mourn or weep at his wife's death, indicating sanctification involves obedience despite emotional hardship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Ezekiel 24:14 specifically demonstrate?
options: Immutability
Omniscience
Mercy
Patience
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:14's declaration that God will not repent or spare shows His immutability—the unchanging nature of His purposes.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Ezekiel 24:8 specifically demonstrate?
options: Justice
Omnipresence
Love
Faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:8 states God sets the blood upon the rock to ensure vengeance, demonstrating divine justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:1-2 connect to the broader biblical narrative of exile?
options: It marks the historical onset of Jerusalem's siege, fulfilling prophetic warnings of exile
It predicts the eventual restoration without judgment
It ignores the exile and focuses on temple rituals
It describes the fall of Babylon instead of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the historical onset of Jerusalem's siege, fulfilling prophetic warnings of exile
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:1-2 records the day the king of Babylon set against Jerusalem, fulfilling the prophetic theme of exile as judgment (cf. 2 Kings 25).

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:21-23 prefigure the New Testament teaching on communal judgment?
options: It illustrates corporate responsibility and shared consequences for sin
It teaches individual salvation without communal accountability
It denies any connection between personal and national sin
It emphasizes ritual purity over moral accountability
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates corporate responsibility and shared consequences for sin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:21-23 shows Israel suffers together—no mourning or covering lips—indicating communal judgment that echoes NT themes of corporate sin (e.g., 1 Corinthians 12).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezekiel 24:12 and Ezekiel 24:13 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Persistent sin leads to irreversible judgment until God's fury is satisfied
God's judgment can be reversed if people repent quickly
Sin is insignificant compared to God's mercy
God purges sin immediately upon confession
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent sin leads to irreversible judgment until God's fury is satisfied
questions.explanation: Verses 24:12-13 emphasize the city’s scum remains until God’s fury rests, teaching judgment is certain and lasts until divine wrath is exhausted.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezekiel 24:17 and Ezekiel 24:22 teach about prophetic symbolism and obedience?
options: Prophets enact symbolic actions as obedience to God's command and as signs for the people
Prophetic symbolism is optional and unrelated to obedience
Prophets must always express traditional mourning rituals
Symbolic actions negate the need for verbal prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets enact symbolic actions as obedience to God's command and as signs for the people
questions.explanation: Both verses command Ezekiel and Israel not to mourn but to perform symbolic acts, showing obedience and serving as prophetic signs.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezekiel 24:26 and Ezekiel 24:27 teach about prophetic communication and divine revelation?
options: God will open the prophet’s mouth to communicate His message clearly after the exile begins
Prophets remain silent throughout times of judgment
Divine revelation ceases after the judgment begins
Prophetic messages are only for the priestly class
questions.correctAnswer: God will open the prophet’s mouth to communicate His message clearly after the exile begins
questions.explanation: Verses 24:26-27 promise Ezekiel will speak to the escaped survivors, showing God’s sovereign timing in prophetic revelation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ezekiel 24:16-18 demands emotional suppression that is unhealthy. What does Ezekiel 24:16-18 actually teach?
options: The passage commands prophetic obedience as a sign to Israel, not a denial of genuine grief forever
It forbids all emotional expression in all circumstances
It teaches that grief is sinful and must be avoided
It suggests that mourning is unnecessary because death is unimportant
questions.correctAnswer: The passage commands prophetic obedience as a sign to Israel, not a denial of genuine grief forever
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:16-18 orders Ezekiel to refrain from mourning publicly as a prophetic sign, not a permanent denial of natural grief.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 24:9 teach about God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment is severe and consumes the guilty entirely
God’s judgment is mild and symbolic only
God does not punish cities but individuals only
God delays judgment indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is severe and consumes the guilty entirely
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:9 speaks of making a great pile for fire to consume the city, illustrating the severity and completeness of divine judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse Ezekiel 24:11 specifically demonstrate?
options: Holiness
Omnipotence
Patience
Immanence
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:11 describes burning and melting out filthiness and scum, reflecting God's holiness and purifying justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ezekiel 24:3 and Ezekiel 24:4 teach about God's use of prophetic imagery?
options: God uses vivid, concrete imagery to communicate complex truths about judgment
God prefers abstract, vague language to obscure His intentions
Prophetic imagery is meant to comfort rather than warn
Imagery is irrelevant to understanding divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God uses vivid, concrete imagery to communicate complex truths about judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 24:3-4 use the metaphor of cooking a pot with choice pieces and bones to symbolize Israel’s judgment, showing God’s use of tangible imagery.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 24:15-18 prepare the reader for understanding prophetic obedience in the face of tragedy?
options: It models Ezekiel’s obedience to God’s command despite personal loss, teaching prophetic faithfulness
It shows that prophets are excused from obedience when grief strikes
It discourages prophets from engaging emotionally with their message
It implies prophets should prioritize personal feelings over divine commands
questions.correctAnswer: It models Ezekiel’s obedience to God’s command despite personal loss, teaching prophetic faithfulness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 24:15-18 narrates Ezekiel’s compliance with God's instructions during his wife’s death, exemplifying faithful prophetic obedience.
